summary: 32 ft steel fire tower with wood cab on Blue Job Mountain, Farmington (Strafford County), NH; built 1915, new cab 2008, NHLR-registered 2002, still in state service.

facts.design: 32-foot steel tower with wooden observation cab (10 by 10 ft); further cab added 1970-1980 per Historic Structures
facts.agency: NH Dept. of Resources and Economic Development

staffing.status: Staffed by the State of New Hampshire sometimes (NHLR visit report)

access.note: The cabin is open to the public on weekends from 11am to 5pm at times of moderate and high fire risk; the deck below the cab offers views at other times (Trailspotting, 2025).

visit.drive_up: Large trailhead on First Crown Point Road with free parking (Trailspotting)
visit.trail_note: Hikers start at the First Crown Point Road trailhead. The south tower trail is the steepest route up, and the northern tower trail descends on an old asphalt service road.

events.note: First used for fire detection by the state Forestry Commission; Historic Structures says 1912-1913
32-foot steel tower with 10-by-10-foot wooden cab constructed at the summit
State established Blue Job State Forest
Stairs replaced the ladder to the cab, 1929-1930; visitation rose afterward
New cab added above the original, which became an open observation platform; adds about eight feet (Historic Structures dates this 1970-1980; NHLR says modified in the 1980s)
Lookout phoned in a hay fire burning on a truck in a field to the Rochester fire department
New tower cab installed during the year (FFLA New Hampshire chapter report)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Historic Structures says first used for fire detection in 1912-1913; NHLR and Trailspotting give 1913. Record year 1913; story says 1912 or 1913.
NHLR and Trailspotting give 32 ft. Historic Structures says a cab added around 1970-1980 raised the tower about eight feet. No height_m is set because the sources do not agree on the total.

NHLR says modified in 1930 and again in the 1980s; Historic Structures gives stairs 1929-1930, a rebuilt cab 1940 and a new cab 1970-1980. The record uses the detailed Historic Structures dates and keeps the NHLR wording in the notes.

notes_for_editor: Brief's 2002 registration and 2008 cab replacement check out (NHLR; FFLA 2008 chapter report says a new cab was installed). Brief's record has no built year or height; built 1915 is supported by NHLR, Historic Structures and the 1915-1916 state report quoted on Forest Lookouts. Height conflict: 32 ft (NHLR, Trailspotting) versus roughly 40 ft if the 1970-1980 cab addition is counted (Historic Structures); no height_m set. First-use year 1912 or 1913 is unresolved. The NHLR 2016 visit report and the Trailspotting 2025 hours are the only current-condition sources; the NH state staffing claim is from the 2016 visit. The 1948 hay-fire item is from Forest Lookouts and spells the town Stratford; it is cited as a fire the lookout reported, names of private officials omitted. Town spelling: Farmington (Historic Structures, Trailspotting) with Strafford County (NHLR). Wikipedia was read as a lead; its town and county lines agree but it is not cited. Page budget: six distinct pages read, one WebSearch.
